description: AequilibraE is an open-source transport modelling package for Python, and a QGIS plugin, that covers the classic four-step toolchain: network building and manipulation (including import from OpenStreetMap and GTFS), trip distribution, path computation, static traffic assignment with several equilibrium algorithms, public transport assignment and route choice. It is developed by the AequilibraE developers on GitHub and PyPI; version 1.7.0 was released on 3 August 2026 and development continued in September 2026. It is location independent: models can be built for any region, and its algorithms can be used directly on pandas and NumPy objects without a full project. The licence is MIT with an added clause requiring reference to the software in documentation of work developed with it; it is free. Caveats: it provides static, not dynamic assignment and no microsimulation, and calibration data (counts, surveys) must come from elsewhere. It supports network flow, capacity planning, optimisation and resilience studies such as link-closure analysis; it complements the dynamic and agent-based models SUMO, MATSim and UXsim catalogued here and reads OpenStreetMap and GTFS data.
